Tbh, I didn't quite get the life-changing hype that surrounding it for years. The internet pedestal made it hard for it to completely blow my mind (definitely because of goated music and meme).

That being said, this game is undeniably well-made.

You can feel Toby Fox’s sheer passion in every single pixel. There is zero half-assed effort here and no spot left untouched. Every single choice, outcome, and bizarre detail feels like it was carefully thought out and intentionally crafted. The characters feel like the main characters of their own lives rather than just background noise, and your choices actually carry real weight.

Plus, the soundtrack is genuinely fantastic and carries so much of the game's spirit.

It might be a bit unfortunate that I played it so late, but I respect the hell out of the work put into this. If you appreciate games crafted with absolute heart and meticulous detail, it’s worth the play.

A true indie masterpiece. Playing Undertale in 2024 shows how well this game has held up since its 2015 release. It's so fun to play; the constant breaking of the fourth wall gives me shivers or makes me laugh every time.

The story (I played the neutral-pacifist and true pacifist routes) is wholesome, goofy, and heartwarming. The characters are just as charming. Every main character can bring a tear of joy, especially near the end. Even the regular mobs are funny enough to keep you entertained and invested.

I have mixed feelings about the genocide route. Yes, it's there, but personally, I don’t think it's a route you'd want to take. It’ll most likely just leave you feeling hollow.

I truly hope more people experience games with real soul, like Undertale. It won't take much of your time but will definitely leave you smiling and feeling a bit silly! :)

11/10. Some music tracks still make me bawl my eyes out when I listen to them without context. The game itself still makes me bawl my eyes out when I replay it, no matter how many times I do.
It still amazes me how a story premise I couldn't have cared less about - monsters vs humans, destroy the barrier to escape - was delivered so brilliantly and so passionately that it's stuck with me for years, that it carved a little hole in my heart and set camp there, with full intention to stay.
It definitely is a brilliant piece of media, and an inspiring force for me. I'll end up listening to some of the soundtrack, or replay the game a bit, and I'll feel an overwhelming sense of "this is so wonderful, and oh how I'd love to make something so wonderful myself some day!"
It's a rare feeling, and one I cherish dearly.
Thank you.

Also unlike other games, this game allows you to spare monsters. Don't forget there is always that option.

Its an awesome game, and just to be short:

Pros:

1) Great music, seriously, haven't heard a videogame with such a big number of memorable songs in a long time.
2) Good story and clearly explained
3) Memorable characters, in a short time of gameplay it manages to get the characters to be well defined and likeable.
4) The gameplay is very original, a nice mix between RPG, a platformer and a bullet hell game.

This is why its one of the best 2D games ever.

Cons:
The only downside seems to be a some of the fans (the very vocal and cancerous ones), not unusual in many popular series, and while a lot of fans created really cool stuff (arranged music versions, animations based on boss battles and even fanmade boss battles) there is quite a few fans that are lost in their obsession for the series and spam trash content from it constantly.

My recommndation is to ignore the bad rep some of the members in the fanbase have given to the series and just trying the actual game for yourselves and see why its one of the highest rated games ever.

Just Cause 3 is an excellent open world experience. The sidescrolling perspective and excellent soundtrack, alongside the lack of a complex story makes this a very good platformer to play when you are very bored. The inclusion of Paper Mario was exciting, yet they didn't do much with it. I had a lot of fun leveling up Ichiban and the party over time, and the minigames were lovely. I got very absorbed in the sidequest where I had to give the young man green potions so he could become stronger. Keeping my pikmin alive was stressful yet very enjoyable. My favorite character was easily Mr. Game & Watch. Charlotte's moveset was great for zoning and easy to understand. I'm shocked a VR game could look this good and run this well. The car list was very very good, and progression from Japanese tuners to Italian exotics felt amazing. I plan to go to the major tournaments in my area for this game. So, case in point, please buy Metal Gear Rising: Revengeance, it's absolutely worth your time

It's very rare for someone like myself to avoid spoilers for a nearly 10 year old game that has had a supposedly massive impact, and now I can say I understand why.

The game has a wonderful set of characters, a banger soundtrack, and massive replay value and secrets. I'd argue that's true even if you get spoiled on this game. Controls for a keyboard are a bit unconventional at first and the game has no settings menu but nothing you can't get used to.

Surprisingly, the game also is really fun to play with friends watching you, especially if they are very passionate about this game.

Simply, the thought that was put into this game is THE reason I would recommend it.

Althought pixelated, Undertale offers a unique experiences to the players.
It's defeninetly worth getting, even if you d'ont like pixelated/retro games, this will probably appeal to you.
Gamers young and old, should try this game at least once.
